title: A Good Plan is Hard to Find: Aligning Models with Preferences is Misaligned with What Helps Users

bias_targets.methodology: Using linear regressions to test if surface-level features like step count and mean words per step predict user and model preferences versus actual objective helpfulness.
Measuring if lexical word overlap between the prompt question and the generated plan influences human or model preference judgments.
Analyzing whether formatting and stylistic cues, specifically lexical diversity (type-token ratio) and Flesch readability scores, predict preferences without correlating with helpfulness.
Qualitative analysis of execution traces to identify instances where users incorrectly judge familiar problem-solving strategies as more helpful than unfamiliar but objectively better ones.
